findings.evidence: Message about "maximum of 30 characters" placed "directly below the postal code field"
findings.fix: Verify which field this message actually applies to and move it to the correct location, or clarify if this postal code field has unusual length requirements.
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - first message
findings.violation: Postal codes in most countries have much shorter limits (typically 5-10 characters). Either this message belongs on a different field or the field type is wrong.

findings.evidence: "Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502."
findings.fix: Replace this message with guidance appropriate for a server error (e.g., "The server is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a few moments.") and remove the suggestion to correct a field.
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - second message
findings.violation: HTTP 502 is a server error (Bad Gateway), not a validation error. Users cannot fix a server error by correcting a form field.

findings.evidence: Placement described as "requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page"
findings.fix: Reposition this message inline with the password field so users can see both the requirement and the field simultaneously.
findings.location: Password reset, new password - first message
findings.violation: This placement creates a usability problem where the message is outside the visible area while the field requiring the information is visible, forcing users to scroll to understand the requirement.

findings.evidence: Message text says "Change this file to one of those formats and upload it again" but Suggested fix states "offers a convert and retry action in place of the message"
findings.fix: Update the message to explicitly offer the conversion action: "Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only. Convert this file to one of those formats, or select a different receipt."
findings.violation: The message tells users to convert the file format but doesn't mention that a conversion tool is available, creating a gap between the message and the intended solution.
